text:
sara: seeing ~8-12% packet loss from nodes in us-west1-b since 23:05 UTC, GPU attach failures on a subset of pods, tail 502s from runtime. Not widespread but concentrated to a few racks. filing here before we escalate.
oncall-bot: alert: network_e2e_packet_loss detected in us-west1-b (severity: medium). Affected services: inference-runtime, kv-cache. See https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123
ben: can you paste a quick sample of the 502 logs? are these new kernel ooms or network flaps?
sara: quick snippet:
```
2026-03-18T23:04:12Z runtime svc: downstream error: 502 Bad Gateway, dial tcp 10.11.5.23:9000: i/o timeout
2026-03-18T23:04:17Z kubelet: failed to attach GPU to pod inference-x34: device not found
```
mira: looks like intermittent egress. I see BGP neighbor flaps on leaf-12 in the fabric. packet loss spikes align with the log times. not all racks, likely a routing flap.
devops-ci: running quick health checks: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=pool=usw1-b` -> 18/24 pods Ready, 4 CrashLoopBackOff, 2 Pending (GPU attach).
ashley: if we start evacuating pods from the affected racks, remember we'll need warm cache in destination to avoid large latency spikes. cost warning: cross-AZ data transfer will spike if chat workloads hit embeddings cache fallbacks.
ben: proposal: soft-drain affected nodes (taint + eviction with grace 300s) -> shift 25% of traffic away using router weights to other us-west1 AZs -> stand up 2 additional preemptible GPUs in us-west1-c for buffer. Thoughts?
sara: +1 to soft-drain. can we do graceful KV warmup (force prefetch) on primary keys for active sessions before redirect?
mira: we can prime top-100 prefix keys via `cache-tool prefetch --keys-file top100.txt --region us-west1-c` but that will increase write/io. we should do it in small batches.
devops-ci: automation note: `./ops/az-evac.sh --nodes node-[a4..a7] --mode soft --grace 300` will taint + evict with cordon. I can run that when we agree.
ashley: about the preemptible plan: preemptibles are cheap but higher churn. prefer 1-2 dedicated burst instances if we need stable capacity for next 2-3 hours.
nate: ops checklist: 1) mark affected nodes as scheduling disabled; 2) adjust router weights by -30% on us-west1-b via `routerctl route set --zone usw1-b --weight 70`; 3) enable fallback model variant with lower memory footprint for evicted pods; 4) monitor token latency and SLO impact.
ben: who's taking coord? sara you saw the logs.
sara: I'll take runbook and start the drain on the two worst racks. mira can handle cache prefetch, ashley will spin burst instances, nate can hold routing changes and watch traffic.
mira: starting prefetch in micro-batches now. will report back on eviction safety after first 50 keys.
ashley: provisioning 2 dGPU burst nodes (s-rtx:dedicated) in us-west1-c, ETA ~7m. will post machine IDs when ready.
devops-ci: ack queued job for soft-drain: target nodes node-a4,node-a5. will respect grace 300s.
oncall-bot: note: creating temporary incident channel #incident-1965004321 for voice coordination.
ben: also flag to finance: we might burn on-demand for ~2-4 hours. sara please add rough estimate once we know how many sessions migrate.
sara: running `kubectl drain node-a4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` now. evictions starting.
mira: prefetch stage 1 done (50 keys), cache hit-rate improved for primed keys by +18% in us-west1-c.
nate: changed router weights: us-west1-b -> 70%, us-west1-c -> 115% (temporarily), us-west1-a unchanged. watching 5xx and p95.
ashley: burst nodes up: ids gpu-uw1c-21,gpu-uw1c-22. added to pool and registered with kube. please avoid full model loads until warm cache in place.
sara: evictions completed on node-a4, pods rescheduled to us-west1-c and us-west1-a. seeing two sessions with elevated tail latency (~500ms -> 1.2s) but throughput stable.
ben: thumbs up. let's keep monitoring for 20m. if more racks show same pattern, we'll consider a partial zonal evacuation.
mira: fabric team is investigating leaf-12. they suspect fiber flap that affects egress path to our transit. ticket TC-314 opened.
ashley: cost note: if we keep burst nodes for >6h, finance says push for reserved short-term instances. I'll create a ticket.
devops-ci: health after action: 24/24 pods Ready in targeted pool. runtime 5xx reduced from 1.4% -> 0.12% in last 10m.
oncall-bot: update: incident severity downgraded to low. Recommended actions: keep extra capacity warm for 1 hour, fabric team to provide remediation ETA.
ben: great work. postmortem owners: sara + mira. add timeline and ops steps. finance will get cost delta from ashley.
sara: noted. I'll start timeline draft after we confirm leaf-12 remediation. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
